status: experimental interoperability architecture; no treaty/legal-recognition claim
purpose: Allow two institutions or trust domains to explicitly recognize bounded classes of credentials, proofs, roles, or attestations for defined purposes without creating automatic transitive trust, imported authority, or universal equivalence.
core_invariants: recognition of a credential or proof does not create execution authority
recognition does not imply legal equivalence outside the declared scope
transitive trust is denied unless separately and explicitly established
recognition may narrow but never silently widen local assurance or privacy requirements
each party retains local revocation, refusal, and consequence-specific policy
withdrawal affects future reliance prospectively without erasing historical evidence
amendments that widen recognized claim classes, purposes, assurance, data scope, or authority-relevant context require explicit renewed acceptance
nonclaims: This profile does not create an international treaty, accreditation, license portability guarantee, or legal recognition regime.
Recognition of evidence is not recognition of every claim by the issuing institution.
Recognition does not grant membership, office, eligibility, benefits, or runtime authority.
This profile does not require a blockchain, DID method, PKI, or credential standard.
